title: 20 free walk-in public dental clinics
summary: Labor would open 20 free public dental clinics (14 in Melbourne, six in regional Victoria) from July 2027, offering walk-in check-ups, fillings, root canals and extractions for adults and children, open 9am–9pm weekdays and 9am–5pm weekends.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Deliver 20 New Dental Clinics
excerpt: 14 clinics will be in Melbourne with six in regional Victoria, and they’ll open from July 2027. It’s a $230 million investment that we can afford.

title: Sign-on bonuses for dentists joining the public system
summary: Labor would pay sign-on bonuses of $20,000 for dentists joining the public system in metropolitan Melbourne and $30,000 in regional Victoria, to staff the new free dental clinics.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Deliver 20 New Dental Clinics
excerpt: Dentists will receive $20,000 to join in metropolitan Melbourne, or $30,000 in regional Victoria. It’s a $5 million investment

title: Weekend emergency care at 10 existing public dental clinics
summary: Labor would open 10 existing public dental clinics on weekends for emergency dental care, including in Ringwood East, Box Hill, Sunbury, Berwick, Springvale, Hoppers Crossing, Bairnsdale, Wangaratta, Seymour and Horsham.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Expand Weekend Emergency Dental Care
excerpt: That’s why a re-elected Carroll Labor Government will open 10 existing public dental clinics on weekends for emergency care.

title: Expand Smile Squad free dental check-ups to kinders
summary: Labor would extend the Smile Squad school dental program to 3,000 preschools and long day care centres, which it says would give 80,000 four- and five-year-olds free dental check-ups.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Expand Smile Squad Dental Vans to Kinders
excerpt: Labor will invest $37.8 million to expand Smile Squad to kinders. It will benefit 3,000 preschools and long day care centres across Victoria.

title: Expand 12 hospital emergency departments with 250 beds and 750 nurses
summary: Labor's 'Slash ED Wait Times Plan' would expand emergency departments at 12 hospitals by hiring 1,500 health workers (including 750 nurses) and adding 250 beds; Labor says this would cut ED wait times at those hospitals by up to 20 per cent.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Slash ED Wait Times by up to 20%
excerpt: It’s a $1.5 billion investment in public hospitals – ongoing, not a short-term fix.

title: 100,000 extra planned surgeries in public hospitals
summary: Labor would fund 100,000 additional planned (elective) surgeries in public hospitals, including evening and weekend theatre sessions, plus 500,000 additional specialist appointments; Labor says this would halve the surgery waiting list, with 30 per cent of surgeries in regional Victoria.
costing: $1.17 billion for surgeries plus more than $195 million for specialist appointments
sourceTitle: 100,000 More Public Surgeries - In Public Hospitals
excerpt: That’s why Labor will invest $1.17 billion deliver 100,000 extra surgeries – and slash the waiting list in half. We’ll also invest more than $195 million for 500,000 additional specialist appointments.

title: 500 extra graduate nurses and midwives; nurse prescriber scholarships
summary: Labor would hire 500 additional graduate nurses and midwives, including subsidising 300 graduate places ($132 million over four years), and fund 200 scholarships for registered nurses to train as prescribers ($1.7 million over four years).
costing: $132 million over four years (graduate places); $1.7 million over four years (prescriber scholarships)
sourceTitle: Labor Will Hire 500 More Graduate Nurses and Midwives
excerpt: Our boost will subsidise 300 graduate nurse and midwifery places in health services across Victoria. That’s a $132 million investment over four years – not a short-term fix.

title: Legislated nurse-to-patient ratios for mental health wards
summary: Labor would extend legislated nurse-to-patient ratios to acute adult, child and youth mental health units, recruiting almost 160 more mental health nurses and funding 30 graduate mental health nurse places.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Deliver Better Mental Health Care with Nurse-to-Patient Ratios
excerpt: That’s why a re-elected Carroll Labor Government will deliver nurse-to-patient ratios for mental health nurses. And we’ll make it law.

title: Mental health, alcohol and drug ED hubs in Bendigo and Shepparton
summary: Labor would build mental health, alcohol and drug hubs in the Bendigo and Shepparton (Goulburn Valley Health) emergency departments, adding eight and six treatment spaces respectively, so every region has such a hub.
sourceTitle: More Mental Health and Drug Support in Bendigo and Shepparton
excerpt: This $84 million investment means every region in Victoria will have a hub – just as the Royal Commission recommended.

title: No out-of-pocket costs for abortion care under 16 weeks
summary: Labor would pay participating public and private providers so that medical and surgical abortion care under 16 weeks' gestation has no consultation, imaging, testing or medication fees, and would extend the medical abortion window to 10 weeks.
sourceTitle: An Abortion Can Cost $1,000 – Labor Will Change This
excerpt: That’s why a re-elected Carroll Labor Government will eliminate out-of-pocket costs for abortions across Victoria.

title: Up to $500 rebate for non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT)
summary: Labor would provide a state rebate of up to $500 per pregnancy for non-invasive prenatal testing, paid directly to pathology labs with no gap, and make 6-week pregnancy scans free at Sexual and Reproductive Health Hubs.
sourceTitle: Prenatal Testing Costs $500 - Labor Will Make It Free
excerpt: Labor will provide a state rebate of up to $500 for NIPT for every pregnancy in Victoria.

title: Increase Victorian Patient Transport Assistance Scheme subsidies
summary: Labor would expand the Victorian Patient Transport Assistance Scheme for regional patients, raising the fuel reimbursement from 21 to 35 cents per kilometre and moving to a flat $125-per-night accommodation subsidy.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Close the Regional Health Gap
excerpt: The fuel reimbursement will jump from 21 cents per kilometre to 35 cents per kilometre.

title: Workplace Protection Orders and security grants for hospitals
summary: Labor would extend the Workplace Protection Orders scheme to hospitals, allowing violent or abusive people to be banned for up to 12 months, and provide grants for hospital lighting, CCTV, duress alarms and secure areas.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Keep Health Workers Safe At Work
excerpt: A WPO will limit or ban violent and abusive offenders from hospitals for up to 12 months

title: Suspend Ambulance Victoria membership of patients who abuse paramedics
summary: Labor would allow Ambulance Victoria to suspend or cancel the membership of patients who are violent or abusive towards ambulance workers, making them liable for ambulance costs, alongside a new patient charter.
sourceTitle: Threaten Paramedics? You’ll Pay
excerpt: Patients who are violent or abusive towards ambulance workers would have their membership suspended or cancelled

title: 25,600 new homes reserved for first home buyers
summary: In partnership with the Commonwealth, Labor would build 25,600 houses, townhouses and apartments across more than 20 locations, reserved for first home buyers for a period after completion and sold at market prices, with the first homes expected in 2027.
sourceTitle: Labor will Build 25,000 Homes for First Home Buyers
excerpt: That's why a re-elected Carroll Labor Government will build 25,600 new homes and reserve them for first home buyers.

title: Supported housing for adults living with severe mental illness
summary: Labor would fund ongoing wraparound support to help adults with severe mental illness maintain tenancies in supported housing after leaving acute care.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Deliver Supported Housing For Victorians Living With Mental Illness
excerpt: That’s why a re-elected Carroll Labor Government will invest $15.8 million to deliver supported housing for adults living with mental illness.

title: Cap public transport fares at $30 a week for two years
summary: From 1 January 2027, for two years, Labor would cap public transport fares at $30 a week ($15 for concession holders); free travel for under-18s and free weekend travel for seniors would continue. Labor says regular commuters would save more than $1,400 a year.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Cap Public Transport Fares at $30 A Week
excerpt: It will start Jan 1 when half-price fares are scheduled to end – and run for two years.

title: Cap tolls at $30 a week in 2027 via quarterly rebates
summary: For 2027, Labor would rebate tolls paid above $30 a week per vehicle on CityLink, EastLink and the West Gate Tunnel (cars, motorbikes and light commercial vehicles), capped at $350 a week and $5,000 per vehicle, claimed via Service Victoria; small businesses could claim for up to five vehicles. Labor would also allow electronic toll notices to avoid paper-bill administration fees.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Cap Tolls at $30 A Week
excerpt: The maximum you can claim for these rebates is $350 per week – or $5,000 over the full year.

title: Restore $300,000 land tax threshold over six years
summary: Labor would reverse the 2023 land tax threshold change, lifting the threshold from a $50,000 site value back to $300,000 in $25,000 annual steps from 2027–28, fully restored in 2033–34; Labor says more than 250,000 Victorians would no longer pay land tax.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Cut Land Tax to Help with the Cost of Living
excerpt: Labor’s land tax changes will cost $230 million over five years.

title: Three-year stamp duty moratorium for restructuring discretionary trusts
summary: Labor would legislate a three-year stamp duty moratorium for eligible discretionary trusts restructuring in response to Commonwealth tax changes, with eligibility based on the Commonwealth's rollover relief.
sourceTitle: Labor Is Backing Business & Delivering Surpluses
excerpt: A re-elected Carroll Labor Government will provide a three-year stamp duty moratorium for eligible discretionary trusts that restructure into alternate arrangements.

title: Review of Absentee Owner Surcharge and Foreign Purchaser Additional Duty
summary: Labor would establish a review of property charges, including the Absentee Owner Surcharge and Foreign Purchaser Additional Duty, examining revenue efficiency, effects on foreign investment in construction and impacts on first home buyers, reporting before the next Budget.
sourceTitle: Working With Industry to Build More Homes
excerpt: Labor will cut land tax and now a re-elected Carroll Labor Government will review the Absentee Owner Surcharge and Foreign Purchaser Additional Duty.

title: $350 million Make It Here Fund for 5,000 manufacturing jobs
summary: Labor would create a $350 million Make It Here Fund ($200 million equity co-investment from uncommitted Innovation Victoria capital and $150 million in industry grants) for advanced manufacturing, food and fibre, health and medical research, and defence; Labor says it would create 5,000 jobs.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Create 5,000 New Manufacturing Jobs
excerpt: The $350 million fund consists of $200 million for equity co-investment and $150 million for industry grants.

title: Make It Here Guarantee: 50% local content for trains, trams and buses
summary: Labor would require every future train, tram and bus procurement to meet a minimum 50 per cent local content target.
sourceTitle: Only Labor Will Make Our Trains, Trams And Buses Here
excerpt: A re-elected Carroll Labor Government will require every future train, tram and bus procurement to meet that target. That’s a minimum of 50 per cent local content

title: Royalties for the Regions fund for mineral royalties
summary: Labor would create a Royalties for the Regions Fund directing 100 per cent of mineral resources royalties (including coal, gold and critical minerals) to regional schools, hospitals and roads, to be locked in in its next budget; more than $500 million is forecast over four years.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Guarantee Royalties for the Regions
excerpt: We will create a dedicated funding pool of mineral resources royalties – including coal, gold and critical minerals. And 100 per cent of it will be protected and invested into the regions.

title: $20 million towards an antimony processing facility in northern Victoria
summary: Labor would invest $20 million towards an antimony processing facility in northern Victoria, which it says would support around 200 construction jobs and 60 ongoing jobs and process up to 5,000 tonnes a year.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Bring Critical Minerals Processing Home
excerpt: Labor will invest $20 million towards Australia’s first antimony processing facility.

title: Pubs to trade until 3am, dogs allowed and faster liquor licences
summary: Labor would give every pub an automatic right to trade until 3am, amend the Food Act 1984 to let publicans allow dogs inside, and set a six-week decision timeframe for standard liquor licence applications.
sourceTitle: Pubs Open Till 3 - And You Can Bring Your Best Friend
excerpt: Under Labor, every pub in Victoria will have the automatic right to trade to 3am.

title: Fix 500,000 potholes and bring road maintenance back in-house
summary: Labor has committed an extra $352 million to double pothole repairs to 500,000 this year, and says it would bring state road maintenance back under government control, create a single road-issue reporting website, set statewide road standards and pilot supervised minimum-security prisoners doing roadside maintenance.
sourceTitle: Taking Responsibility for the Safety of Our Roads
excerpt: If re-elected, Labor will develop a plan alongside experts and local workforces to put government back in charge of state road maintenance.

title: Upgrade 50 local roads, including $893 million for 25 projects
summary: Labor would upgrade 50 local roads and intersections across Victoria, including an $893 million package for 25 projects (19 in regional Victoria) such as duplicating Ballarat–Carngham Road, with planning and construction starting next term.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Upgrade 50 Local Roads
excerpt: Today, we’re announcing a new, $893 million plan to upgrade 25 more local roads.

title: Build Stage 1 of the Bellarine Link near Geelong
summary: Labor would build Bellarine Link Stage 1 with two lanes each way between Surf Coast Highway and Barwon Heads Road ($237 million), with planning from 2027, and upgrade Murradoc Road in Drysdale ($57 million).
sourceTitle: Labor Will Build Stage 1 of the Bellarine Link
excerpt: A re-elected Carroll Labor Government will invest $237 million to deliver the first stage of the Bellarine Link.

title: 10-minute train services on five more Melbourne lines
summary: Labor would run trains every 10 minutes (7am–7pm weekdays, 9:30am–7pm weekends) on the Mernda and Glen Waverley lines and parts of the Hurstbridge, Belgrave and Lilydale lines.
sourceTitle: Turn-Up-And-Go Services On Five More Melbourne Train Lines
excerpt: Labor $100 million investment means trains will run every 10 minutes, seven days a week

title: Increase V/Line services by 24 per cent
summary: Labor would add more than 550 V/Line services a week from 2027–2028, including extra services on the Melton, Wyndham Vale, Geelong, Seymour and Bendigo lines, as part of a more than $1 billion investment in public transport services.
costing: Part of a more than $1 billion investment in public transport services
sourceTitle: More V/Line Services For Our Outer Suburbs And Regions
excerpt: A re-elected Carroll Labor Government will increase V/Line services by 24 per cent. All up, that’s more than 550 additional services every week across every line.

title: Turn-up-and-go buses every 10 minutes in Melbourne's west
summary: Labor would run buses every 10 minutes from 6am to 10pm on key routes in Melbourne's west, seven days a week, with new connections including Werribee Station to Melbourne Airport.
sourceTitle: Buses Every 10 Minutes in the West Under Labor
excerpt: That's why a re-elected Carroll Labor Government will invest $400 million to deliver turn-up-and-go buses across Melbourne's west.

title: $80 million to begin Upfield Line duplication
summary: Labor would spend $80 million over two years on development work (site investigations, design and approvals) to duplicate the single-track section between Gowrie and Upfield, aligning it with delayed level crossing removals on the line.
sourceTitle: Only Labor Will Kickstart Upfield Line Duplication
excerpt: We will invest $80 million over the next two years to kickstart the duplication of the Upfield Line.

title: Continue Suburban Rail Loop with $2 billion targeted savings
summary: Labor would continue building the Suburban Rail Loop, having identified $1 billion in project savings, and is commissioning an independent technical review targeting a further $1 billion in savings.
sourceTitle: Tunnelling Begins On The Suburban Rail Loop
excerpt: Labor has identified $1 billion in immediate project savings and is commissioning an independent technical review to target a further $1 billion in savings.

title: Upgrade 228 public schools and fund non-government school upgrades
summary: Labor would spend more than $1.17 billion to upgrade 228 public schools and plan upgrades at 16 more, plus $500 million for non-government schools ($350 million for Catholic schools and $150 million for other low-fee independent schools, including a $30 million grant round for Islamic schools).
costing: More than $1.17 billion (public schools); $500 million (non-government schools)
sourceTitle: Labor Will Upgrade Hundreds of Local Schools
excerpt: Now, a re-elected Carroll Labor Government will invest more than $1.17 billion to upgrade 228 public schools, and plan for upgrades at 16 more.

title: Two new TAFE campuses and upgrades to three others
summary: Labor would build new TAFE campuses in Wyndham and near Kalkallo ($50 million each) and upgrade TAFE campuses in Bendigo, Wonthaggi and Dandenong ($70 million).
sourceTitle: Liberals Cut TAFE. Labor Made It Free. Now We’ll Build More Campuses.
excerpt: A re-elected Carroll Labor Government will build two new TAFE campuses in Melbourne’s outer north and west.

title: Bring public school cleaning in-house
summary: Labor would employ public school cleaners directly through the Department of Education as current contracts expire at the end of 2027, phasing in from Term 1 2028 across more than 1,600 campuses in 2028 and 2029.
sourceTitle: Secure, Local Jobs for Public School Cleaners
excerpt: Cleaners will be employed directly by the Department of Education and will be part of the local school workforce.

title: $50 million grants to open school facilities for community use
summary: Labor would fund a statewide grants program for security upgrades (up to $150,000) and access works such as fencing and gates (up to $500,000) so public school ovals, halls and courts can be used by community groups after hours.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Open School Facilities to the Community
excerpt: Now, our $50 million statewide grants program will mean more local clubs and community groups can use their great local school facilities.

title: Recruit 1,500 more police and open a police academy in Wyndham
summary: Labor would recruit 1,500 additional police, open a second permanent metropolitan police academy in Wyndham, support triple-squad graduations and speed up recruitment for people such as ADF veterans and PSOs.
sourceTitle: Only Labor Has a Real Plan to Recruit a Full Police Force
excerpt: That’s why, if re-elected, we will open a second metro police academy – in Wyndham.

title: Jack's Law statewide knife stop-and-search powers
summary: Labor would legislate 'Jack's Law – Stop and Search', allowing police to use handheld metal detectors to search for knives in any public place without declaring a designated area, in place statewide by early 2027, with 1,200 additional handheld detectors.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Implement 'Jack's Law' Stop and Search Powers
excerpt: Jack’s Law – Stop and Search will be in place statewide by early 2027

title: 200 more police reservists and six new or upgraded police stations
summary: Labor would recruit 200 more police reservists (more than $70 million) to staff police station counters, and build or upgrade stations at Watergardens, Doncaster, Keilor Downs, Greensborough, Moonee Ponds and Clayton ($300 million).
sourceTitle: More Police Reservists To Re-Open Stations
excerpt: Now we will go further by investing more than $70 million to recruit 200 more reservists.

title: Youth rehabilitation detention under Mandatory Therapeutic Orders
summary: Labor would legislate a new Mandatory Therapeutic Order allowing courts to sentence low- and mid-level youth offenders to up to 12 months in secure residential youth rehabilitation detention with compulsory education, drug and alcohol treatment and mental health support, starting with almost 500 places over two years.
sourceTitle: Tough Love Plan To Detain And Rehabilitate Youths
excerpt: This is a $204 million investment and an Australian-first. It will start with almost 500 places for youth offenders over two years, and scale up.

title: Life maximum for rape and tougher sexual and family violence laws
summary: Labor would introduce a maximum penalty of life imprisonment for rape, raise maximum penalties for serious sexual offences by five years, set a 30-year standard sentence for murder of a current or former partner, and double the maximum penalty for persistent family violence intervention order breaches to 10 years.
sourceTitle: Toughest Penalties Ever for Rapists and Sex Offenders
excerpt: Introduce a new, standard sentence of 30 years for murder of a current or former partner

title: $10 million for BlueHub police mental health service
summary: Labor would provide more than $10 million to the Police Association's BlueHub service for police mental health and wellbeing, including new early intervention support.
sourceTitle: Labor's Plan for a Full Force - In Full Health
excerpt: A re-elected Carroll Labor Government will back BlueHub with more than $10 million in support.

title: 2km buffer between new waste-to-energy projects and homes
summary: Labor would introduce a 2-kilometre buffer between the boundaries of new waste-to-energy projects and existing homes; it would not apply to currently operating facilities.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Keep Waste to Energy Away From Homes
excerpt: A re-elected Carroll Labor Government will introduce a 2-kilometre buffer between new waste-to-energy project boundaries and existing homes.

title: Add wine bottles to Container Deposit Scheme; purple bin optional
summary: Labor would add glass wine bottles to Victoria's 10-cent Container Deposit Scheme and make the purple glass recycling bin optional for councils rather than mandatory by July 2027.
sourceTitle: Wine Bottles To Join Container Deposit Scheme
excerpt: A re-elected Carroll Labor Government will add glass wine bottles to Victoria’s Container Deposit Scheme. Labor will also make the purple glass bin optional for councils.

title: Victorian Land Use Commissioner to protect farmland
summary: Labor would establish a Victorian Land Use Commissioner, supported by specialist advisers, to advise government on farmland protection and publicly report on pressures facing agricultural land.
sourceTitle: Labor Will Protect Victoria's Farms
excerpt: a re-elected Carroll Labor Government will establish a Victorian Land Use Commissioner, supported by a specialist team of advisers. This is a $6 million investment.

title: Royal Commission into the construction sector with Special Prosecutor
summary: Labor says it is funding the Royal Commission into the construction sector (led by former SA Chief Justice Chris Kourakis) with up to $50 million and a 12-month reporting timeframe, backed by an independent Special Prosecutor and strengthened powers to compel information.
sourceTitle: Royal Commission into the Construction Sector
excerpt: Labor is funding the inquiry with up to $50 million and has asked it to report within 12 months, so Victorians get thorough and timely answers.

title: 150 new fire trucks for FRV and CFA by 2030
summary: Labor would deliver 150 new fire trucks by 2030 (50 FRV trucks, 50 CFA pumpers/pumper-tankers and 50 CFA tankers), manufactured in Victoria, and commits that no FRV truck operates beyond 15 years' service life by 2035.
sourceTitle: 150 New Fire Trucks for the Frontline to Keep Us Safe
excerpt: We will deliver 150 new fire trucks by 2030.

title: Live music precincts, Live Music Desk and $2.5m Live Gigs Fund
summary: Labor would create live music precincts with reformed noise rules (including Fitzroy, Collingwood, Geelong and Ballarat), a permanent Live Music Desk, a $2.5 million Live Gigs Fund and $1.5 million to activate underused spaces, and require Victorian music in government advertising.
sourceTitle: If You Move House Next to Live Music, Expect Live Music
excerpt: We will create targeted live music precincts in inner Melbourne and regional Victoria, including Fitzroy, Collingwood, Geelong and Ballarat.

title: $80 million Victorian Racing Industry Fund
summary: Labor would renew and increase the Victorian Racing Industry Fund to $80 million (up from $72 million) for thoroughbred, harness and greyhound racing infrastructure, regional events and animal welfare.
sourceTitle: Only Labor Will Protect Racing Jobs
excerpt: An $80 million investment will help grow the sport and support grassroots racing across Victoria.

title: Free miner's right for recreational prospecting
summary: Labor would make recreational prospecting and fossicking free from next year by removing the fee for a miner's right; existing rules on where people can prospect would remain.
sourceTitle: Labor Is Making It Free to Go For Gold
excerpt: A re-elected Carroll Labor Government will make recreational prospecting and fossicking free from next year
